keyword: the distribution of the sensible (le partage du sensible)
concept_purpose: Names the shared aesthetic substrate of art and politics: an a priori system of perception that partitions the visible/invisible and audible/inaudible, deciding who counts as a speaking, visible member of a community.
paper_title: Empire of rain: Rancière, Béla Tarr, and the politics of the sensible
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues this concept is the indispensable scaffolding for reading Béla Tarr as a political filmmaker: by directing his long takes at abject, marginal Hungarian subjects, Tarr does not represent a predefined group but creates a people out of those who remain invisible and inaudible, redistributing sensory attention.

concept_purpose: The mechanism that makes the distribution of the sensible political: a disruption of consensus that brings the sensory experience of neglected subjects to the fore and contests who has the ability to see and the talent to speak.
paper_title: Empire of rain: Rancière, Béla Tarr, and the politics of the sensible
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Reads Tarr's films as enacting dissensus through form: an opposition of two sensible worlds (Krasznahorkai's nihilistic narrative vs. the long-take mise en scène; cyclical repetition vs. the straight line), embodied in Estike's walk, which reopens time as the site of the possible.

concept_purpose: A historical-aesthetic paradigm that abolished art-as-mimesis, fusing art and life and creating a sensible community irrespective of the artist's intent, theorised as an alternative to the concept of modernity.
paper_title: Empire of rain: Rancière, Béla Tarr, and the politics of the sensible
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues Rancière positions Tarr's 'time after stories' as exemplary of the aesthetic regime against both modernism and postmodern end-of-history pathos, while critically charging Rancière with instrumentalising Tarr to substantiate his own fable about the aesthetic regime.

concept_purpose: Traces the shift from sovereign power to disciplinary mechanisms and then to environmental forms of governance, where biopower modulates the conditions within which subjects act rather than coercing bodies directly.
paper_title: Through the looking glass: The biopolitics of digital becoming
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues the avatar-subject relationship is the privileged site of environmental biopower: screen interfaces produce cybernetic milieus that govern subjectivity by continuously adjusting spaces of potential (exemplified by the game Echochrome), a real-time feedback that exceeds Foucault's original formulation.

concept_purpose: Reformulates biopolitics as having an immunitary structure that simultaneously safeguards and constrains life by introducing the very negation it aims to prevent.
paper_title: Through the looking glass: The biopolitics of digital becoming
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues the avatar enacts immunitary logic exactly: it protects the subject by mediating exposure to digital environments yet entails dispossession of the subject's image and behaviour; the character Bella Baxter in Poor Things is read as affirmative biopolitics reclaiming the immunitary apparatus.

concept_purpose: Names the sovereign power to dictate who may live and who must die, reducing populations to 'death-worlds' of living death; operates alongside biopower to determine which lives are optimised and which abandoned.
paper_title: Through the looking glass: The biopolitics of digital becoming
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Coins the 'necropolitics of the digital' to name the systematic extraction of value from the living through the commercial resurrection, algorithmic reanimation, and political manipulation of their dead data-doubles within platform infrastructure.

concept_purpose: Theorises the passage from disciplinary societies (operating on the bounded individual) to control societies that modulate dividuals: decomposable, reconfigurable data-profiles that are simultaneously more and less than persons.
paper_title: Through the looking glass: The biopolitics of digital becoming
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues the avatar is the dividual in its most legible form: a decomposable, commercially exploitable data-entity that maps the transition from the disciplinary society's bounded subject to the control society's modulated dividual.

keyword: cadaverous resemblance / the image as corpse
concept_purpose: Holds that the image precedes the object and bears a fundamental relationship to death, revealing the thing as absence; the corpse is its own image, a presence constituted through absence.
paper_title: Through the looking glass: The biopolitics of digital becoming
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Theorises the avatar as a corpse-image whose agency is essentially posthumous, generating 'algorithmic necromancy' and 'zombie agency'; extended via Derrida's hauntology, the avatar continues to act on and extract value from the living subject whose absence it marks.

concept_purpose: A decolonial ethics opposing the demand for transparency: opacity affirms the irreducible singularity of the Other and builds horizontal relations that do not appropriate or convert the Other into one's own image.
paper_title: Disappearing to appear: Towards a politics of opacity in contemporary European audiovisual culture
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues contemporary European audiovisual depictions of migration and diasporic identity can mobilise a politics of opacity, refusing the regime of visibility/legibility that would render migrants knowable and governable, so that disappearing becomes a mode of appearing on one's own terms.

theorist: Sebastian Scholz (building on Harun Farocki's operational images and Gilbert Simondon's milieu)
concept_purpose: Names how sensing media operate within dense, entangled environments ('au milieu') where operation and exchange preclude fixed identities, requiring analytic cuts to render mediating processes sensuously perceptible.
paper_title: On mediating environments: Sensor-milieus and operational aesthetics
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues environmental sensor media constitute 'sensor-milieus' whose operational aesthetics must be interrupted and translated to be understood; analysis must begin in the midst of entangled processes rather than from stabilised objects or subjects.

concept_purpose: Grounds perception in the lived, embodied body rather than a disembodied eye, holding that spatial representation is never neutral but produced through an embodied perceptual apparatus.
paper_title: Getting 'up close…at a safe distance': Transparency and opacity in the weaves of VR
journal: NECSUS: European Journal of Media Studies
paper_argument: Argues VR's hyperreal 3D spheres are not neutral spaces but are produced through the phenomenological apparatus of Western Man and colonial cartographic techniques; weaves of transparency and opacity in VR works are read as critiques of that spatial regime.

concept_purpose: A history and theory of 'visuality' as the authority of the visual field used to police and naturalise power, against which Mirzoeff posits a counter-'right to look'.
paper_title: Notes on visuality and the Policing Complex
journal: Jump Cut: A Review of Contemporary Media
paper_argument: Theorises post-Ferguson policing technologies as a 'Policing Complex,' a concept derived from Mirzoeff's history and theory of visuality, to show how surveillance imagery sustains the authority of the police state.

theorist: Teshome Gabriel (extending Fernando Solanas and Octavio Getino)
concept_purpose: Third Cinema theorises a militant, anti-colonial cinema aligned with popular memory against 'official history,' opposed to both Hollywood (First) and auteurist art (Second) cinema.
paper_title: Notes on 'Third Cinema as guardian of popular memory'—an Indian context
journal: Jump Cut: A Review of Contemporary Media
paper_argument: Analyses how Teshome Gabriel extends Third Cinema's potential as guardian of popular memory in the conflict between official history and popular memory, applying it to Indian film, literature, and culture.

concept_purpose: Names the delegation of one's own passive enjoyment or belief to another agent or object, where the medium consumes or believes in the subject's place.
paper_title: Disco Elysium and the intersection of interactivity and interpassivity
journal: Jump Cut: A Review of Contemporary Media
paper_argument: Argues the 2019 RPG Disco Elysium suggests a new model of interactivity precisely by incorporating interpassivity into the gaming experience, complicating the assumed agency of the player.

concept_purpose: The panopticon models disciplinary surveillance where the few watch the many; Mathiesen's synopticon names the inverse mass-media condition where the many watch the few.
paper_title: Between panopticon and synopticon in the late period films of Stéphane Brizé
journal: Jump Cut: A Review of Contemporary Media
paper_argument: Through close readings of Brizé's workplace dramas La Loi du Marché and En Guerre, contributes to debates on surveillance under late capitalism by reading the films between the poles of panoptic and synoptic visibility.

concept_purpose: Melodrama theory explains the moral legibility and excess of popular narrative; Jameson's postmodernism names the cultural logic of late capitalism marked by fragmentation and depthlessness.
paper_title: Everything just goes black: time, melodrama, and narrative incompleteness in The Sopranos
journal: Jump Cut: A Review of Contemporary Media
paper_argument: Argues The Sopranos reconfigures the melodrama for the era of postmodern capitalism through its network of symbols, codes, and fractured temporalities, culminating in narrative incompleteness.

concept_purpose: Theorises settler colonialism as a structure not an event, driven by a 'logic of elimination' of the native to make claims on stolen land.
paper_title: Beyond an Asian settler cinema: Asian American media, PBS, and the settler colonial state
journal: Jump Cut: A Review of Contemporary Media
paper_argument: Conceptualises Asian American media on PBS as a settler colonial media movement complicit with the settler state's claims to stolen land and citizenship, reframing Asian American media history beyond a purely anti-racist narrative.

theorist: Christian Keathley & Jason Mittell (parametric); Lisa Samuels & Jerome McGann (deformance)
concept_purpose: Constraint-driven, procedural modes of videographic criticism that generate insight by manipulating and remixing image and sound according to predetermined rules rather than explanatory voiceover.
paper_title: Men Shouting: A History in 7 Episodes
journal: [in]Transition: Journal of Videographic Film & Moving Image Studies
paper_argument: Deploys parametric and deformative techniques on three American films about the 2008 financial crisis, arguing that parametric criticism need not be recuperated into conventional argument but can access an affective, poetic dimension of cinema on its own terms.

theorist: literary autofiction concept (Serge Doubrovsky lineage), applied to screen media
concept_purpose: A hybrid mode blending autobiography and fiction in which an author stages a version of the self oscillating between authentic confession and fictional construction.
paper_title: Autofictional Authenticity: Bo Burnham's Inside, Netflix Comedy and YouTube Aesthetics
journal: [in]Transition: Journal of Videographic Film & Moving Image Studies
paper_argument: Frames Bo Burnham's Inside as autofiction that continually oscillates between puncturing and indulging authentic confessional modes, situating it among proto-mockumentary, confessional stand-up, and the manufactured authenticity of YouTubers.

theorist: Timotheus Vermeulen & Robin van den Akker
concept_purpose: A structure of feeling defined by oscillation between modernist sincerity and postmodern irony, theorised to characterise post-postmodern cultural production.
paper_title: Autofictional Authenticity: Bo Burnham's Inside, Netflix Comedy and YouTube Aesthetics
journal: [in]Transition: Journal of Videographic Film & Moving Image Studies
paper_argument: Argues a metamodern sensibility explains Inside's constant oscillation between sincere confession and ironic self-reflexivity, distinguishing its manufactured authenticity from straightforward documentary.

concept_purpose: Names how discrete, beloved image-moments function as transferable affective modules that accrue and shift emotional resonance as they are repeated and recontextualised across remix and fan culture.
paper_title: On the Art of Affective Repetition: Fan Video & The Untamed
journal: [in]Transition: Journal of Videographic Film & Moving Image Studies
paper_argument: Uses The Untamed and its transcultural fanworks to argue that logics of modular affectivity sit at the heart of remix and fan culture, as official and fan authors repeat and recontextualise image-moments that gather new emotional resonance.

concept_purpose: Theorises vidding as a fan remix practice of music videos that reedit source footage to produce critical and affective interpretation, central to remix culture.
paper_title: On the Art of Affective Repetition: Fan Video & The Untamed
journal: [in]Transition: Journal of Videographic Film & Moving Image Studies
paper_argument: Positions the analytic fan video within the vidding/remix tradition, arguing transcultural fans rework the Chinese source by combining it with referents from their own cultural contexts, demonstrating remix as transcultural interpretive practice.

theorist: Barbara Zecchi (resonant with Rosalind Krauss on the grid)
concept_purpose: The grid as a visual structure that both disciplines/contains and, by fracturing, releases—used to figure the social discipline of women's rage and its transformation into solidarity.
paper_title: The Rhythms of Rage: From Solitude to Solidarity
journal: [in]Transition: Journal of Videographic Film & Moving Image Studies
paper_argument: Assembles 500+ clips into a shifting multiscreen grid, arguing the grid operates as both structure and rupture: social constraints discipline women's rage while rhythmic montage can fracture those constraints into feminist solidarity, mapping a trajectory from solitude to solidarity.

theorist: Allan Sekula (counterforensics), extended via Thomas Keenan
concept_purpose: Inverts the state's forensic gaze: turning forensic and evidentiary methods against the violence committed by the very institutions (police, military, courts) that normally wield them.
paper_title: Striking Evidence: A Counterforensics of Courtroom Assemblies
journal: World Records
paper_argument: Examines courtwatchers' drawing, writing, and marking ('scrivening' or 'Common Paper') by Court Watch NYC and NYU students as a counterforensic record of resistant courtroom assemblies that is obscured from Anglo-American jurisprudence.

concept_purpose: Recovers the classical sense of 'forensis' as the practice of making objects and environments speak in a public forum, developing forensic aesthetics as a means of investigating state and corporate violence.
paper_title: They Are Shooting at Our Shadows
paper_authors: Al-Haq Forensic Architecture Investigation Unit and Rachel Nelson in conversation with Laliv Melamed and Pooja Rangan
journal: World Records
paper_argument: Through the Al-Haq Forensic Architecture investigation, interrogates how forensic aesthetics can be reoriented toward abolitionist and decolonial aims in documenting violence against Palestinians, and the limits of evidence under occupation.

theorist: Yasmina Price (building on Saidiya Hartman's critical fabulation)
concept_purpose: Names how Black memory, conjured in tongueless whispers and recited choreographies, forms a link between living and dead that no forensics can capture, intervening in how the past is encoded and inherited.
paper_title: Tongueless Whispers and Recited Choreographies
journal: World Records
paper_argument: Argues contemporary Afro-diasporic artists model an 'aesthetic counterforensics' in their audiovisual work to combat the colonialist and imperialist foundation of traditional evidence-based depictions of Black life.

theorist: Başak Ertür & Alisa Lebow (extending Allen Feldman)
concept_purpose: Names how state agencies survey and reconstruct bodies and events to produce control, and how the forensic gaze can itself perpetrate violence against the dead and the marginalised.
paper_title: Countering Forensic Violence: Philip Scheffner's Revision
journal: World Records
paper_argument: Reads Philip Scheffner's film Revision—revisiting the 1992 killing of undocumented Roma workers on the German-Polish border—as a documentary practice that counters forensic violence by refusing the state's reconstructive gaze and restoring agency to the dead.

theorist: Guy Standing (the precariat), applied to platform creative work
concept_purpose: Theorises a class-in-the-making defined by insecure, casualised labour without stable income or benefits, generalised by the platform/gig economy.
paper_title: Game Design for a Fiverr: Precarity, Platform Labor, and the Creative Class
journal: Media Industries
paper_argument: Examines how platforms such as Fiverr casualise creative game-design labour, forcing workers into increasingly precarious arrangements, situating freelance game work within wider debates on platform labour and the gig economy.

concept_purpose: Reframes how scholars conceptualise competition among video services, moving beyond the 'streaming wars' framing to analyse the structural economics of the platform video market.
paper_title: Beyond Streaming Wars: Rethinking Competition in Video Services
journal: Media Industries
paper_argument: Argues the 'streaming wars' metaphor obscures the actual dynamics of the video-services market and proposes rethinking competition through a more structural political-economic account of platform rivalry and market position.

theorist: Karin van Es & Ramon Lobato (VoD catalogue and interface analysis methods)
concept_purpose: Develops methods to study streaming catalogues and interfaces as infrastructures of cultural visibility, treating discoverability and catalogue composition as objects of critical data analysis.
paper_title: Exploring VoD Services through Data Donations: A View from Netflix
journal: Media Industries
paper_argument: Uses data-donation methods to investigate Netflix's catalogue and interface, arguing that critical analysis of VoD infrastructures reveals how platforms shape discoverability and cultural visibility beyond what corporate metrics disclose.
